mainTopic: Why the פסוק about pouring the leftover blood of the נשיא's חטאת onto the base of the outer מזבח must be teaching something extra
overview: This amud continues a דרשה on the פסוק about the חטאת of a נשיא (a king). That פסוק says the leftover blood (שירים) is poured at the base of the 'מזבח העולה.' The דרשה reads these words as 'give a יסוד to the מזבח of the עולה,' meaning the base for leftover blood belongs to the outer מזבח. The גמרא then proves the פסוק must be teaching this wider rule. Read plainly, it would only be teaching something obvious: the blood of this חטאת is already placed on the outer מזבח, so of course its leftovers go there too. The amud ends as the גמרא starts to suggest a reason the פסוק might still be needed for its own case: maybe one would think the כהן reverses the procedure. That suggestion is dealt with on the next amud.

steps.title: The teaching: the base belongs to the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: The דרשה reads the פסוק as teaching that the outer מזבח, the מזבח of the עולה, is the one with a יסוד where leftover blood is poured.
steps.simpleTranslation: Give a base to the altar of the burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the lesson it learns from the words 'יסוד מזבח העולה': the יסוד for leftover blood belongs to the outer מזבח, the מזבח of the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'pour it on the יסוד.' By linking the יסוד to the 'מזבח העולה,' the דרשה turns it into a general rule: leftover blood from any offering goes to the base of the outer מזבח. The next step proves the verse must be read this way.

keyTerms.meaning: The base: the bottom ledge of the outer מזבח, where leftover blood is poured
The altar of the burnt offering, which is the outer copper מזבח in the courtyard

phrases.english: Give a base to the altar of the burnt offering.
phrases.notes: This reads the end of ויקרא 4:25, 'יסוד מזבח העולה,' as a general rule about where leftover blood goes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the דרשה from the end of the previous section of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'יסוד מזבח העולה' teach that the יסוד for pouring leftover blood belongs to the outer מזבח.

steps.title: Proof that the verse is not needed for its plain meaning
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only meant its own case, it would be useless. The blood of this חטאת is already put on the outer מזבח, so of course the leftovers go there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if you think the verse means just what it says, about this offering alone, why do I need these verses? To teach about the leftover blood? But the main placements of blood are already done on the outer altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it has to read the פסוק as a general rule: read plainly, the פסוק would be telling us something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נשיא's חטאת is an outer חטאת, so its blood is placed on the outer מזבח. No one would think its שירים go to the inner מזבח, so a פסוק saying 'pour them on the outer מזבח' adds nothing. Since the תורה does not waste words, the פסוק must be teaching a wider rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind: introduces an idea the גמרא is about to show cannot be right
As it is written: in its plain meaning only
The leftover blood that remains after the required placements on the מזבח
Outside: the outer מזבח in the courtyard

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic 'אם אינו ענין' move: when a פסוק is not needed for its own case, the גמרא uses it to teach a broader rule.

phrases.english: Because if it enters your mind that it means just as it is written,
phrases.notes: He means: as if the verse were only teaching about the נשיא's חטאת itself.

phrases.english: why do I need these verses? For the leftover blood?!
The leftover blood? But he does the placements outside, on the outer altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves that the דרשה in step 1 is necessary by showing the plain reading is pointless.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that 'יסוד מזבח העולה' teaches a general rule and not just its own case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that an outer חטאת's leftover blood obviously goes to the outer מזבח, so the verse would be extra

steps.title: A suggestion: maybe the כהן switches the order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to offer a possible reason the verse is needed even for its own case: maybe one would think the כהן reverses the procedure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that the priest reverses the placements...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a possible answer to the question 'why is the verse needed?' The sentence breaks off at the end of this amud and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that someone might think the procedure gets switched around, so the verse is needed to keep the leftover blood at the outer מזבח. The phrase 'וכי תימא' signals that the גמרא will likely reject this suggestion next.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a possible answer, usually about to be rejected
He actually reverses: switches the order or place of the procedure

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's conclusion. 'וכי תימא' just raises a possibility that the גמרא is about to answer in the next lines.

phrases.english: And if you would say that he actually reverses them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense of the plain reading against the proof in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proposed reason the verse might be needed even for its own case (setup, likely to be rejected)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse is pointless for its own case, since the outer placements make the outer שירים obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe it is needed because one might think the כהן reverses the procedure. This is still to be evaluated in the next section.
